encoding_policy.input_encoding: none - the report splits the psv line on '|' bytes and never decodes. Exports are written back as ISO-8859-1 so a Latin-1 or byte-shifted UTF-8 name round-trips to the same bytes the legacy wrote
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: full: currency and record-type labels are raw byte strings, so 'usd' and 'USD' stay different groups and UNKNOWN(<raw>) keeps the raw value including trailing spaces
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: none rejected; the CSV is written unquoted and unescaped exactly as the legacy does, so a comma inside a value corrupts the file in both systems

malformed_record_policy.details: Aggregation reads positional fields 1, 5 and 6 of the re-split psv line, so a delimiter collision shifts the group key. That is reproduced (C-5.1). Rows whose field 1 is empty are skipped (C-7.2). A row with an empty currency and record type still forms a group, keyed on the empty string, and sorts last.

empty_input_semantics.details: With no parsed input the report is written header-only - 'Currency,RecordType,RecordCount,TotalAmount' plus LF, no data rows, no error (C-7.8). The gold table is emptied for the run, not left stale.

acceptance_checks.description: Gold rows equal the captured CSV row for row: currency, record type label, record count and total amount, compared on the raw group key.
Money is exact. A one-cent difference is a failure, not a tolerance. Totals are summed in DECIMAL(38,2), not float.
Row order matches ASCII byte order of the raw 'currency|rec_type' key: digits before uppercase before lowercase, and the empty key last (C-7.5).
Label mapping is exactly 01->INVOICE, 02->CREDIT, everything else->UNKNOWN(<raw>) with trailing spaces preserved (C-7.4).
The exported CSV is byte-identical to the captured legacy CSV, header included, LF line endings, no quoting.
The exported .xls is byte-identical to the exported CSV; it is not a workbook and is documented as such (C-7.11).
The report aggregates every parsed file retained, not a single day's slice, so totals are cumulative and grow every run (C-7.1).
A second run writes byte-identical outputs and leaves gold row counts unchanged, proven by an actual rerun.

planted_anomalies.description: The report is cumulative over every retained psv file, so the 'daily' finance close silently restates all history and the Sunday run_all re-run re-emits the same totals under a new filename.
Grouping is on raw bytes, so 'usd' and 'USD', and '1 ' and '01', are different groups in the same report.
The CSV is written with no quoting or escaping, so a comma in any value corrupts the file.
The .xls is a byte copy of the CSV produced by `cp`, so the extension misrepresents the format to every consumer that opens it.
Totals are accumulated as IEEE doubles, so above abs(total) ~9.0e13 the legacy loses cents while the DECIMAL target does not.
planted_anomalies.reason: The fixture set totals ~5e5, six orders of magnitude below the divergence bound, and inflating amounts to reach it would not be the legacy's real data. The bound is derived (C-7.9) and reported as an anomaly if a live total ever approaches it.

planted_anomalies.description: Output is mailed through a sendmail pipe whose binary has been absent for years; the failure is swallowed, so nobody has received this report in years and nobody noticed.
